details.description: ERNIE-4.5-21B-A3B-PT is an instruction-tuned language model from Baidu's ERNIE 4.5 family, released as open weights in Transformer-style PyTorch format (the '-PT' suffix distinguishes it from Baidu's PaddlePaddle-format release of the same checkpoint). It uses a heterogeneous mixture-of-experts architecture with 21B total parameters and 3B activated per token, drawn from 64 text experts (6 active per token) plus 64 vision experts and 2 shared experts across 28 layers, and is trained for text generation in English and Chinese. Baidu reports it achieves competitive performance against Qwen3-30B-A3B despite having roughly 30% fewer total parameters.
advantages: Baidu reports it achieves competitive performance against Qwen3-30B-A3B despite having roughly 30% fewer total parameters.
Uses a mixture-of-experts architecture that activates only 3B of its 21B total parameters per token, reducing inference cost relative to a dense model of similar quality.
disadvantages: Baidu's own model card does not publish quantitative benchmark score tables for this specific variant.
Documented for English and Chinese only; broader multilingual support is not stated.
use_cases: General text generation and instruction following in English and Chinese
Tasks where a smaller active-parameter MoE model is preferred over a larger dense model for efficiency

sources.title: ERNIE 4.5: Baidu's new open model family

notes: Bud's catalog lists a 4,096-token input/output limit for this model, but Baidu's model card states a native context length of 131,072 tokens; kept the catalog's figure per instructions and did not restate 131,072 in the description. Found no numeric benchmark table specific to the 21B-A3B variant, only qualitative comparisons to Qwen3-30B-A3B, so evaluations is left empty rather than guessed. Corrected the Qwen3-30B-A3B comparison: Baidu's blog attributes the 'outperforms on math/reasoning benchmarks including BBH and CMATH' claim to the ERNIE-4.5-21B-A3B-Base checkpoint, not this post-trained -PT release; the post-trained model is only described there as achieving 'competitive performance ... despite having approximately 30% fewer total parameters,' with no benchmark domain specified.
